This is not a shotgun wedding. They do not plan to have kids for the foreseeable future (if ever.) They intend to have a proper wedding in the future, when finances allow. However, in the meantime, she's forbidden me from mentioning it to anyone in our family or even friends of mine who know her, but do not know the family. These are kids who never had an apartment and want us (the parents) to give them what they need to get started. It's a financial imposition to ask us to furnish their house, and I know that both my family and the groom's family would be delighted to help if they could. In addition, the groom's family all knows this is going to happen and I feel our family will be terribly hurt if they are shut out completely. We're not inviting people to the courthouse, obviously, but they can call and offer their Congratulations anyway. I'm worried that, when they finally do have their wedding, nobody will want to come because they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. Further, I make lots of crafts and baked goods. I like to post the projects on social media for critiques and she's forbidden me from posting the wedding cake picture. Her real wedding will have a professional cake, but I wanted the practice, around just a few of us will be there. Frankly, my enthusiasm for helping her is dwindling and I am contemplating *not* baking the cake, as literally this exposure was all I wanted. I'm also thinking of offering her less for setting up house. My original thinking was, they could save up faster if they don't have to buy furniture and dishes. But she won't let us enlist the help of others. We have to replace what we give her and do without in the meantime, because we don't have money to buy these things right now. We're willing to do this for their comfort. It sure would be nice to see if anyone else is planning on getting rid of some old furniture or dishes so they can get started. Am I being an asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me break it down step by step. First, my daughter is getting married next week to her boyfriend of two years. It's not a shotgun wedding, and they plan to have a proper wedding in the future when they can afford it. Right now, they're getting married at the courthouse while he's on leave from the army. They don't plan to have kids for the foreseeable future, so they're starting their life together without that immediate pressure. Now, the issue is that my daughter has forbidden me from telling anyone in our family or even our friends who know her but not the family about the wedding. She also doesn't want me to post any pictures of the cake I'm baking for the courthouse ceremony on social media. I make a lot of crafts and baked goods, and I usually post them online for feedback. This cake was just a practice, and only a few of us would be there, but she's against me sharing it. I'm feeling hurt because I want to share this milestone with our family and friends. I also think that if we don't let people know now, when they finally have their proper wedding, no one might want to come because they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. Plus, I'm considering not baking the cake because she's so against me sharing it, and that's really disappointing. Financially, they're asking us to help furnish their house, which is a big imposition. I know that both our family and the groom's family would be happy to help if they knew. The groom's family already knows this is happening, so I feel like our family is being shut out completely. We're not inviting people to the courthouse, but they could call and offer congratulations. I'm worried about the hurt feelings if they're excluded. I also want to help them set up their house by giving them furniture and dishes so they can save money. But my daughter doesn't want us to involve others, so we have to replace what we give her, which means we're doing without in the meantime. I'm thinking of offering less help because of her restrictions, which is making me less enthusiastic about helping her. I'm also considering whether anyone else is planning to get rid of old furniture or dishes so my daughter can get started without buying new things. But again, she doesn't want us to involve others, so it's hard to know. So, am I being an asshole? I don't think so. I'm trying to support my daughter, but I feel like she's being unreasonable by not letting me share this important news with our family and friends. I also feel like she's not considering the hurt feelings of our family by excluding them. Plus, she's making it harder for us to help her by not allowing us to involve others or share our efforts online. I think it's reasonable to want to share such a significant event with loved ones. It's also important to consider the feelings of others and not exclude them, especially when they might be willing to help. I'm not trying to control her life, just to share in her joy and get the support from our community. So, I don't think I'm being an asshole; I'm just trying to navigate this situation in a way that's fair to everyone involved.
